description: Attack the two largest ABSOLUTE costs: shape6 (n4096 B2, 14.6ms) and shape5 (n2048 B8, 8.7ms) -- together a big chunk of wall time. Prior runs called the n4096 recon path 'floored' because its FP64 Cholesky (cusolverDnDpotrf) is SIMT with tensor cores idle; that is a reason to REPLACE it, not stop. Build a tensor-core mixed-precision solver: blocked Cholesky whose bulk trailing SYRK/GEMM runs on TF32 (or FP16) tensor cores with FP64 only on the tiny diagonal blocks, plus 1-2 steps of iterative refinement to recover FP32 accuracy. Apply the same to the n2048 path. Validate HARD on shape5/6 + cond0/upper stress; confirm with interleaved A/B. Profile custom_kernel IN ISOLATION. NEVER use 'timeout' or any shell-timeout wrapper -- the harness auto-backgrounds long commands.

ISOLATION DISPROVES the brief's mechanism on B200: (1) accuracy FAIL -- orth gate margin 210x@nb256 -> 5172x@nb1024 because cond(G)~3e8 needs FP64 in the trailing Schur; 3xTF32 (~FP32) loses small eigenvalues, worse with wider nb; 1 IR step cannot recover 2.5 orders. (2) speed FAIL 7835-9470us vs cuSOLVER FP64 3544us (per-block Dpotrf + hi/lo + FP64-subtract overhead; trailing GEMMs underfill 148 SMs at B=2). ROOT CAUSE: FP64 is FAST on B200 -- FP32 Spotrf only ~18% faster than Dpotrf and ~0 end-to-end (chol is launch/bandwidth-bound, not FP64-FLOP-bound), and FP32 chol end-to-end fails orth 153x. The mature n4096 path is already tensor-core (INT8-Ozaki Gram, 3xTF32 solve). Stage split: Gram 12%, chol 24% (~0 wall delta fp32/fp64), solve 16%, RECON 49% = the real headroom.

(2) Plain FP32 Spotrf for n4096: orth 153x over gate, ~0 wall gain (FP64 is FAST on B200 -- Spotrf only ~18% faster than Dpotrf, chol is launch/bandwidth-bound NOT FP64-FLOP-bound; the 'SIMT-FP64 floored' framing is from older GPUs and is FALSE here). (3) Routing n2048 B8 to CholeskyQR = 2.1x REGRESSION (18667 vs 8717us Householder): chol balloons to 7421us (~928us/matrix, no batch fill) and recon to 7724us at B8. The mature kernel's routing (n4096->CholeskyQR, n2048->Householder) is already optimal. WHERE THE REAL SHAPE6 HEADROOM IS: stage split of the n4096 CholeskyQR path is Gram 12% / chol 24% (but ~0 wall delta fp32-vs-fp64) / solve 16% / RECON (orhr_col) 49%. The recon dominates -- a next brief should attack the orhr_col reconstruction (recon_lu_cpp blocked-LU + build_H), e.g. wider TF32 trailing, fewer diag_lu launches, or a cheaper Householder-reconstruction formulation, NOT the Cholesky. For shape5 (n2048) the panel kernel is the cost (58.6%, one-CTA/matrix at 8/148 SMs); a multi-CTA-per-matrix panel m-split would help more than any Gram-based path.

The trailing-GEMM precision wall is FUNDAMENTAL (V^T@C cancellation on ill-conditioned inputs blocks reduced precision -- disproven repeatedly). So stop attacking precision; attack the ROUTING. shape7 (n512 mixed) flags ~bad matrices and runs the WHOLE bad subset through the exact-FP32 path. But within the bad subset, only the genuinely ill-conditioned columns need FP32 -- the well-conditioned LEADING columns of each bad matrix could still use the fast BF16 path. Try a finer-grained split: instead of per-MATRIX good/bad, do per-COLUMN-BLOCK precision -- run the leading well-conditioned panels of bad matrices in BF16, switch to FP32 only for the trailing ill-conditioned columns (detect via the existing rank-reveal/column-norm machinery).
